### 🟡 Changes recommended The synthetic batch envelope lacks a property map, allowing propagation to fail with a null-pointer exception before delegation.
2 open findings - [Initialize synthetic envelope properties before starting instrumenter](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20479#discussion_r4242827044) · New - [Remove redundant cast when passing count to equalTo](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20479#discussion_r4242827065) · New
What changed in this PR Adds a RocketMQ producer wrapper that injects context before batch encoding, restoring propagation for newer clients. **Changes:** - Adds `RocketMqTelemetry.wrap(DefaultMQProducer)` and deprecates hook-only producer instrumentation. - Adds batch propagation, lifecycle, failure, and integration coverage. - Updates javaagent wiring and usage documentation. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `CHANGELOG.md` | Records the API deprecation and replacement. | | `.../​testing/​.../​AbstractRocketMqClientTest.java` | Routes sends through the configured producer wrapper. | | `.../​library/​.../​RocketMqProducerWrapperTest.java` | Tests wrapper behavior and batch propagation. | | `.../​library/​.../​RocketMqClientTest.java` | Configures library tests with the wrapper. | | `.../​library/​.../​TracingSendMessageHookImpl.java` | Coordinates hooks with wrapper-owned send state. | | `.../​library/​.../​RocketMqTelemetry.java` | Exposes the wrapper API and deprecates the send hook API. | | `.../​library/​.../​RocketMqProducerWrapper.java` | Implements producer delegation and pre-encoding propagation. | | `.../​library/​.../​RocketMqProducerAttributeGetter.java` | Reports wrapper batch message counts. | | `.../​library/​README.md` | Documents wrapper-based usage. | | `.../​javaagent/​.../​RocketMqClientTest.java` | Adapts javaagent tests to the shared producer contract. | | `.../​javaagent/​.../​RocketMqSingletons.java` | Uses the helper-created send hook. | | `.../​javaagent/​.../​RocketMqBatchSendHelper.java` | Constructs single-message hook instrumentation directly. |
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

[General] `createProducerInstrumenter` injects through `MapSetter` during `instrumenter.start(...)`, and that setter calls `envelope.getProperties().put(...)`. A default RocketMQ `Message` has no initialized property map, so an instrumented collection send can throw before reaching the producer. Initialize this synthetic envelope's properties (or otherwise prevent propagation into the envelope) before starting the instrumenter.
[Testing] `equalTo(AttributeKey<Long>, int)` already supports this value, so the explicit cast is redundant; pass `count` directly.

<!--
CHANGELOG.md is generated from merged pull requests. Do not add an entry unless this PR introduces
a deprecation or breaking change.
-->

Fix RocketMQ library batch propagation by injecting context before the client encodes the messages, rather than re-encoding them in a send hook.

Configure a `DefaultMQProducer`, then wrap it once for both single-message and batch sends:

```java
MQProducer producer = telemetry.wrap(configuredProducer);
producer.send(message);
producer.send(messages);
```

Deprecate `RocketMqTelemetry.createSendMessageHook()` in favor of `wrap(DefaultMQProducer)`. The old hook stays functional, but hook-only integrations must adopt wrapping to get the batch propagation fix.

Use collection-based `send` overloads for batches; already-encoded `MessageBatch` objects are not re-encoded. Consumer hooks and javaagent batch instrumentation remain unchanged.

Fixes #15526.

cc @YaoYingLong
metadata.title: Fix RocketMQ batch propagation with a producer wrapper
